description: Imports recruiting and applicant-tracking data (candidates, applications, jobs, interviews, offers, users) from the Ashby hiring platform.

scheme.passwordField: <none — the connector hardcodes an empty password>

continuity.ourSideLoss: The per-binding Ashby syncToken (the connector's log cursor) expires after roughly a month of disuse; the API then returns a 'sync_token_expired' error and the connector must re-list the entire collection.
continuity.resumeWindow: ~1 month of not using a given stream's syncToken
continuity.notes: Poll-mode HTTP connector; nothing is created or held on the customer's Ashby tenant, so nothing accrues on their side if we stop between ticks. The only continuity risk is ours: an expired syncToken degrades the next run into a full re-listing (handled automatically — the connector drops the token and retries, but only when the failure occurs on the first page of a sync).

discovery.method: Fixed shipped stream list, filtered at discover/validate time by the API key's granted scopes
discovery.querySketch: POST /apiKey.info -> results.scopes; keep each shipped stream whose declared required_scope is present in that set
excludes: Any shipped stream whose required_scope (e.g. offers:read, approvals:read) is absent from the API key's scopes is skipped

authTierRationale: The only credential mode is a single self-serve Ashby API key supplied as `credentials.access_token`. The connector wraps it in HTTP Basic (key as username, empty password) itself; there is no OAuth spec (TokenSource is constructed with oauth_spec=None), no client id/secret, and no refresh token. One value, pasted once.

unionMisfits.description: Pagination is an envelope token that travels in the JSON REQUEST BODY of a POST, not in a query string, header, or next-page URL. The response envelope carries {success, moreDataAvailable, nextCursor, syncToken, errors} alongside results[]; the connector resends envelope.nextCursor as body key "cursor" on the next POST and loops while envelope.moreDataAvailable is true. v2.1's `body_cursor` member covers this, but the member's documented shape does not name the HTTP method, and every other paginator member implicitly assumes GET — a consumer that ignores httpMethod on the PullSpec will silently issue GETs and get page one forever. There is also no page-size or limit knob anywhere in this connector.

The incremental cursor is not a timestamp parameter at all. It is an opaque server-issued `syncToken` read off the response envelope, persisted as the binding's log cursor, and sent back in the JSON request BODY on the FIRST request of the next sync only (never on subsequent pages, which carry `cursor` instead). `incrementalParam` has no body-field variant and no opaque-token format, so it is left null.

proposedShape.onExpiry: drop the token and re-list the full collection

unionMisfits.description: This connector sends ZERO query parameters. The values recorded under `params` are JSON request-body fields (per-stream static flags such as includeArchived / includeDeactivated, plus the injected parent id for child streams). PullSpec has no `body` field, so they are recorded in `params` — a consumer that renders them as a query string will silently drop archived rows and break the child streams.

Parent-scoped streams are scoped by a BODY field, not a path placeholder: the connector lists parents (interview_schedules / interview_plans) and then issues one child POST per parent id with `interviewScheduleId` / `interviewPlanId` in the body. `pathPlaceholders` cannot express this. Additionally, interview_events' incremental cursor is the PARENT's syncToken — the child endpoint itself has no incremental support — so a checkpoint advances only when at least one parent changed.

Ashby has no separate historical sweep. The same function performs both legs: with no stored syncToken the POST returns the entire collection (the backfill), and the envelope's syncToken then makes every later run return only changes. The two PullSpecs here are byte-identical apart from whether `syncToken` is present in the first request body; they are not independently schedulable or independently resumable.

pull.note: backfill is the first invocation of the incremental leg

transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders.snippet:
# Ashby requires Content-Type: application/json on all POST requests.
# Passing json={} ensures aiohttp sets the header automatically.

streams[*].pull.*.httpMethod.snippet: _, response = await http.request_stream(log, url, method="POST", json=body)

discovery.method.snippet:
resources: list[AshbyResource] = [
    _create_incremental_resource(stream_cls, http)
    for stream_cls in INCREMENTAL_STREAMS if _has_required_scope(log, stream_cls, available_scopes)]

discovery.querySketch.snippet:
response = await http.request(log, f"{API_BASE_URL}/apiKey.info", method="POST", json={})
... return set(info.results.scopes)

execution.mode.snippet:
# Since incremental fetches couldn't begin until a complete backfill was performed,
# it is impossible to define two discrete functions — the fetch function does both.
fetch_changes=functools.partial(fetch_fn, entity_cls, http),

unionMisfits[3].snippet:
for parent_id in updated_parent_ids:
    body = {**entity_cls.base_request_body, entity_cls.parent_id_field: parent_id}

abstained.streams[*].cursorField: There is no document-level cursor field. Incrementality is driven by an opaque `syncToken` carried on the response envelope (ResponseMeta.syncToken) and stored as the binding's log cursor; no record attribute is compared against anything (api.py:140-165). Naming any document field here would be invented.
abstained.streams[*].pull.incremental.incrementalP: Not expressible: the incremental token is a body field (`syncToken`) sent only on the first request of a sync, and its format is opaque rather than iso8601/unix_seconds/date. See unionMisfits[1].
abstained.streams[*].pull.*.paginator.pageSize: No page-size or limit parameter exists anywhere in the connector; page size is entirely server-chosen.
abstained.streams[interview_events].cursorField: interview_events checkpoints on the PARENT interview_schedules syncToken, not on anything belonging to the child records (api.py:168-219).
abstained.transports[0].spec.apiVersionPinning: No API version appears in the base URL, in any path, in a header, or as a parameter — paths are bare `<entity>.list` under https://api.ashbyhq.com.
abstained.streams[*].writeDisposition (incremental: Recorded as `merge` from key=["/id"] plus the CDK's default incremental reduction; the connector never emits a delete/tombstone for incremental streams, so hard deletes in Ashby are not represented. Whether Ashby's syncToken feed itself surfaces deletions is not determinable from this repository.
abstained.execution.continuity.releasedOnShutdown: Not applicable/undeterminable: the connector creates no server-side artifacts to release. Left null rather than asserting a behaviour.
abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.passwordField: There is no user-facing password field at all — the connector passes password="" literally. The recorded string is a description, not a config field name.
abstained.streams (completeness): The 24 streams listed are the full shipped set, but a live discovery returns only the subset the API key's scopes permit; a given deployment may legitimately expose fewer.
abstained.streams[7].pull.backfill.params.intervie: Not a literal value: the connector first lists parents via POST /interviewSchedule.list and then issues one child POST per parent id, injecting it into the JSON body under this key. There is no path placeholder — the parent scoping is a body field.
